class.name: AudioEffectSteamSpatial
class.brief_description: Spatializes a point source to stereo using Steam Audio's built-in HRTF.
class.description: Converts a mono point source into binaural stereo from global [member source_position], [member receiver_position], and [member receiver_orientation]. The effect derives Steam Audio's listener-local unit direction internally. The current implementation folds Godot's stereo bus input to mono before spatialization, applies [member gain], and uses Steam Audio's built-in HRTF. This is a render effect only. It does not locate a Godot listener or source, trace geometry, calculate propagation delay, or render reflections and reverb. [AudioStreamQPlayer3D] updates its parameters from Godot transforms. Keeping the unnormalized global transforms at this interface leaves room for a later propagation-delay stage to deliver time-aligned source positions. Place [AudioEffectSteamDirect] before this effect when direct-path filtering is required. Output is always a stereo binaural signal intended for headphones; it is not a loudspeaker-surround decoder.

method.name: set_spatial_parameters
method.description: Updates both global transforms, [member gain], and [member spatial_blend] as one coherent snapshot. This is the preferred real-time update method.

members.member: Source position in the same global coordinate frame as [member receiver_position]. Distance is retained for future delay integration but does not itself apply gain or propagation delay here.
Receiver or listener position in global coordinates.
Global receiver orientation. Its inverse rotates the global source direction into the listener-local direction required by Steam Audio.
Nonnegative linear gain applied to the mono source immediately before HRTF rendering. This is an integration convenience and is not a field of Steam Audio's [code]IPLBinauralEffectParams[/code].
HRTF measurement interpolation used when the derived listener-local direction falls between measured locations.

Blend between unspatialized mono and fully HRTF-spatialized output, clamped to [code]0.0[/code]–[code]1.0[/code]. Because this implementation first folds input to mono, [code]0.0[/code] does not preserve the original stereo image.

constants.constant: Uses the nearest measured HRTF direction. This is the lower-cost option.
Interpolates between nearby HRTF measurements. This is smoother for wide-band material but costs more CPU.
